description: Headnotes for about 1,000 published federal court of appeals decisions, spread across all 13 circuits and across the years, written by Claude agents in a cloud session from CourtListener text with the pilot's prompt. Supplements the Haiku run of headnotes-circuits-v1.

producer.method: Claude agents in a cloud session (about 10 workers in parallel, each taking one court and date window of about 10 decisions), reading each opinion through the CourtListener API; not the Message Batches API.

input.source: CourtListener API, html_with_citations of each cluster's main opinion.
input.paragraph_numbering: Count of block elements in the text read from CourtListener html_with_citations (p, blockquote, author, headings, and blank-line runs in pre text), caption lines included, numbered straight through head and tail when cut. Counted by the writing agent, not by a script. Not build.py's numbering of graph.opinion_text.
input.truncation: Texts over 48,000 characters of html_with_citations were cut like the Haiku requests: the first 36,000 characters and about the last 12,000. Shorter texts were read whole.

selection: 13 circuits (ca1-ca11, cadc, cafc) x 8 date windows each, one random two-month window per era (1930-1949, 1950-1962, 1963-1972, 1973-1982, 1983-1992, 1993-2002, 2003-2012, 2013-2025; ca11 and cafc 8 eras from 1982), seed 20261125. In each window, published opinions from CourtListener search in date order, about 10 per window, extended by up to three further two-month windows when short. Skipped: the 20 pilot clusters, main opinions under 1,500 characters, and duplicate copies of one decision (same reporter citation; the copy with the higher citeCount was kept). selection.jsonl lists every cluster taken, so other runs can skip them.
compare_with: headnotes-circuits-v1 (Haiku run, not yet in this repository)
caveats: The prompt is the pilot's reconstruction from what the Haiku run's transcript showed, not the text of data/prompts/headnotes.md; where the Haiku agents reported a rule differently, the stricter version was used.
Concept slugs are guesses in the style of the headnotes-v2 taxonomy, which was not available; most will fail a slug check until remapped. Compare topics, not strings.

Paragraph numbers were counted by the writing agents over CourtListener's html_with_citations, not by build.py over graph.opinion_text, so treat them as approximate; each headnote's anchors give the first words of the cited paragraphs.

Long opinions were cut like the Haiku requests (first 36,000 and about the last 12,000 characters), but measured in characters of html_with_citations rather than bytes of graph.opinion_text, so the cut falls in a somewhat different place.
The word limit used was 60; the Haiku agents reported limits between 60 and 75.
These decisions were not checked against the Haiku run's request list, so some may also have Haiku answers; selection.jsonl lets the Haiku run skip them or compare.

CourtListener marks many Federal Appendix (F. App'x) decisions from the Caselaw Access Project as Published, so the selection includes them as the search returned them; they are non-precedential, and their citation field shows F. App'x.

CourtListener holds many decisions twice (Caselaw Access Project and Public.Resource.Org copies). The copy with the higher citeCount was taken; its cluster id may differ from the one in the Starfield graph for the same decision.
producer.model is left null in this repository.
extra.selection_window is the date window (see selection) a decision was drawn from; extra.notes are the writer's notes on each decision.
